_meta.semantics: covers_syllabus_refs is an index of the objectives a stage is principally associated with; coverage is claimed only through _syllabus_items + covers_items, and only as far as coverage_check.py confirms.

_items_source.document: The Open University BSc (Hons) Mathematics, qualification Q31, module list and stage structure (module pages at open.ac.uk/courses/modules/<code> and the OU Mathematics and Statistics prospectus), cross-checked against the QAA Subject Benchmark Statement for Mathematics, Statistics and Operational Research (published 2023-03-08)
_items_source.version: Q31 module list and module pages as published on open.ac.uk, itemised 2026-09-27
_items_source.numbering: This course's own stable ids (block.letter, e.g. 4a), grouped into 15 stages, one per named OU module's principal topic strand; the OU's own internal unit-by-unit numbering within each module sits behind the student VLE and is not reproduced.

_syllabus_items.title: Complex numbers: Cartesian and polar (modulus-argument) form, arithmetic and the Argand diagram

Sequences and series: convergence, the ratio test, Taylor/Maclaurin series of standard functions

Stationary points of functions of two variables; classification via the Hessian/second-derivative test
The multivariable chain rule and implicit differentiation
Lagrange multipliers for constrained optimisation
Discrete and continuous random variables; expectation and variance
The binomial, Poisson and normal distributions as models; the Central Limit Theorem
Point estimation, confidence intervals and the sampling distribution of the mean
Hypothesis testing: null/alternative hypotheses, significance level, Type I/II error, p-values
Simple linear regression and the least-squares line
Groups: definition, axioms, examples (Z_n, symmetric groups, dihedral groups, matrix groups)

_syllabus_items.title: First-order ODEs: separable equations and integrating factors for linear equations
Second-order linear ODEs with constant coefficients: complementary function and particular integral
Systems of first-order linear ODEs; solution via eigenvalues/eigenvectors of the coefficient matrix
Phase-plane classification of equilibria for 2x2 linear systems (node, saddle, spiral, centre)
Modelling with ODEs: exponential growth/decay, damped harmonic motion, predator-prey
Scalar and vector fields; grad, div and curl
Line integrals of scalar and vector fields; work done by a force field
Surface integrals and flux; the Divergence Theorem
Green's Theorem and Stokes' Theorem
Rings: definition, axioms, examples (Z, Z_n, polynomial rings, matrix rings)
Integral domains and fields; zero divisors; units
Ideals and quotient rings
Ring homomorphisms and the First Isomorphism Theorem for rings
Unique factorisation in Z and in polynomial rings; irreducibility
Metric spaces: definition, examples (Euclidean, discrete, sup-norm on C[a,b]) and metrics induced by a norm
Open and closed sets; interior, closure and boundary in a metric space
Convergence and continuity in a general metric space; equivalence with sequential continuity
Compactness and completeness in a metric space; a continuous image of a compact set is compact
Complex differentiability and the Cauchy-Riemann equations; holomorphic functions
Power series and elementary functions (exp, sin, cos, log branches) as complex functions
Contour integration; Cauchy's Theorem and Cauchy's Integral Formula
Taylor and Laurent series; classification of singularities (removable, pole, essential)
The Residue Theorem and its use in evaluating real integrals
Likelihood and maximum likelihood estimation
Properties of estimators: bias, consistency, efficiency; the Cramer-Rao bound (statement only)
Confidence intervals via the likelihood/normal approximation and via pivotal quantities
The general linear model; least squares as maximum likelihood under normal errors
Chi-squared tests: goodness of fit and tests of independence in contingency tables
